A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same confidence-sphere research. Their complete text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–F support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 Figure 1 reports confidence-sphere widths calculated from sampled Beta-distributed random vectors, providing original simulation results.

after.justification: v2 Figure 1 reports simulations with Beta variables and beta-binomial mixtures, including variability across 100 trials.

M1.justification: v2 adds Gaussian-based sub-Gaussian confidence spheres, a Gaussian-mixture construction for time-varying means, and a conditional-symmetry construction for heavy tails. It also revises semi-empirical and robust radius formulas. The thresholded Catoni–Giulini estimator itself remains unchanged, moving from Theorem 3 to Theorem 6.

E1.justification: The simulations retain multivariate mean estimation but revise synthetic distribution coverage: v1's Beta(50,10) example disappears, while v2 introduces mixtures of betas and binomials. Uniform and Beta(10,10) examples remain. The new time-varying-mean theory is not accompanied by an empirical evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds an oracle multivariate Bernstein comparator, attributed to Gross (2011) and Kohler and Lucchi (2017), for the bounded-data comparison. The median-of-means comparator remains in the Catoni–Giulini comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds a fixed-time convergence evaluation with alpha = 0.05 and d = 2, and extends the median-of-means comparison from d = 20 to d = 5, 20, and 100. The latter retains the alpha/(t+t²) union-bound procedure. The new Bernstein comparison introduces oracle variance information as a control.

E4.justification: v2 adds a numerical illustration of convergence toward the existing asymptotic-width result and extends the dimension-sensitivity analysis of the heavy-tail comparison. Variance-adaptation illustrations remain, with revised distributions. Neither version reports an empirical contamination-robustness test.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 1 explicitly reports standard-deviation bands across 100 trials. v1 supplies neither corresponding variability bands nor a repeated-run count. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increase in runs for a retained experiment.

E6.justification: v2 adds convergence results, oracle-versus-empirical Bernstein curves for the revised distributions, and heavy-tail comparison curves at additional dimensions. The qualitative findings of variance adaptation and narrower Catoni–Giulini bounds than union-bounded median-of-means remain. These additions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement between versions.

T1.justification: v2 adds sub-Gaussian and conditional-symmetry theorems, the time-varying-mean proposition, and a sub-Gaussian stitching derivation in Appendix A.3. It also corrects substantive mathematics: v1 Appendix C's Gaussian second-moment expression d/β² becomes d/β+1 in v2 Appendix D.2, changing the semi-empirical bound. v1 Appendix B's robust bound with a constant 2C term is replaced by a dimension-dependent bound containing t·epsilon·(exp(C)−exp(−C)), with an explicit proof in Appendix D.3.

C1.justification: The introduction adds claims of tighter sub-Gaussian concentration and an extension to time-varying means, materially broadening the contributions beyond v1's constant-mean constructions. It also qualifies the blanket closed-form claim by explicitly excluding the implicit robust heavy-tail result.

C2.justification: v1 suggests fully empirical heavy-tail bounds as future work; v2 Section 3.1 instead explains why known variance information is necessary and why empirical variance terms may fail to concentrate. v2 also acknowledges dimension dependence of the revised robust construction and explicitly identifies the less favorable dimension/logarithm separation in its stitched bound compared with Manole and Ramdas.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit tuning guidance for new constructions, including the Gaussian precision choice for Corollary 2, epoch weights in Appendix A.3, and constant-weight behavior for robust heavy-tail bounds. Neither PDF provides simulation code, and the new mixtures' component parameters and weights are not fully specified.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially through comparisons with oracle Bernstein bounds, classical sub-Gaussian concentration, and Gaussian-mixture methods, adding works including Gross, Kohler–Lucchi, Jin et al., Rigollet–Hütter, and Robbins. The self-normalized-work discussion is rewritten, and new Appendix C derives the relationship to Wang and Ramdas. Publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: Sections 3 and 4 gain thematic subsections, revised material from v1 Appendices B–C enters the main text, the anisotropy discussion moves to Appendix B, and Catoni proof development moves into Appendix D. The introduction, related work, explanations, and conclusion are extensively revised.

P2.justification: The main figures are redesigned into a three-panel Figure 1 combining convergence, Bernstein comparisons, and heavy-tail comparisons. The original density panel is removed, and uncertainty shading, legends, and a logarithmic time axis are introduced. The vMF plot is retained and renumbered. The heavy-tail legend incorrectly retains 'Theorem 3' although that result is now Theorem 6.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important mathematical deficiencies in v1 Appendices B–C, correcting Gaussian moment calculations and contamination accounting while supplying fuller proofs. These repairs, useful new inferential constructions, and clearer applicability limits substantially improve the paper's reliability and scope. Some revised guarantees are more conservative, appropriately reflecting their assumptions. Incomplete mixture specifications and the stale figure legend remain limited weaknesses.
